correctness.rationale: For every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle, independent Dirichlet(1,1,1) barycentric coordinates yield D²=-(x t₂t₃+y t₁t₃+z t₁t₂). Direct factorial integration produces M₂=e₁/18, M₄=(e₁²-2e₂)/60, and M₆=(23e₁³-62e₁e₂+20e₃)/4200. Exact polynomial inversion then recovers squared side roots; Heron yields 16 area²=e₁²-120 M₄. The stated positive-root and strict-Heron condition is necessary and sufficient for realizability. Root perturbation on connected unions of three complex disks gives uniform normalized Hölder exponent 1/3 and explicit constant <7; an admissible two-family collision with equal first two moments shows the exponent is sharp. The included standard-library checker independently expands all 19 coefficients in exact rational arithmetic and verifies the full formulas and explicit ambiguous pair. Finite examples are not used as a substitute for the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is finite inverse recovery of every triangle, the exact two-moment area identity, a complete cubic realizability criterion, and globally sharp 1/3 inverse stability. Classic formulas for the full random-point distance law and all its forward moments are expressly treated as prior work; the mathematical implications of those forward results do not include a published theorem isolating the particular three point-pair moments as sufficient or identifying their global optimal stability exponent. Older chord-power triangle recognition is a serious specialist comparison: the precise previously reported sufficient data {I0,I1,I5} and the later {I0,I1,I2} are not the same area-normalized point-pair data {I5,I7,I9}. The Gates primary manuscript could not be read in full, and historical priority remains a documented risk. No partition-specific claim of novelty is made.
residual_risks: The original 1982 Gates article is only abstract-accessible; an unpublished or unindexed corollary involving precisely I5,I7,I9 is not excluded.

value.rationale: The problem asks which small number of global, noise-estimable geometric statistics characterize an arbitrary triangle. Two moments determine area exactly but leave continuous shape ambiguity; a third resolves every shape, including isosceles and equilateral cases. A fully explicit test characterizes admissible moment triples, and the globally uniform inverse stability rate of exponent 1/3 is sharp near equilateral triangles. The statistical-geometric invariant is natural and the precision of the sharp conditioning result goes beyond a routine tabulation or moment evaluation.
